title: Vaginal Bleeding

rationale.Transvaginal US: Fetal cardiac activity, GS, retained products.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with vaginal bleeding, cramping lower abdominal pain, and passage of tissue in early pregnancy (<20 weeks). Types: threatened (bleeding, closed os, viable fetus), inevitable (bleeding, open os), incomplete (partial passage of tissue, open os), complete (all tissue passed, os closed), missed (fetal demise without expulsion). Diagnosis: HCG positive, transvaginal ultrasound to assess fetal cardiac activity, gestational sac, and retained products. Serial HCG levels: normally doubles every 48h in early pregnancy — falling or plateauing suggests nonviable pregnancy. If Rh-negative → Rhogam (anti-D immune globulin) to prevent alloimmunization. Treatment: threatened → expectant management, pelvic rest. Inevitable/incomplete: expectant (allow to pass), medical (misoprostol), or surgical (D&C). Complete → confirm with US, no further treatment needed. Emotional support and counseling.
